reuse.why: Routes every expected-amount computation through the existing exported getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts and reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.ts for the approximate tolerance instead of re-deriving 7.5%.

duplication.why: Removes the five inline midpoint copies (forecast-schedules, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, schedule-template) and adds no new copy of the rule.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the other schedule helpers, the API field is computed in the api-models toExternal mapper, and the handler type is updated in types/api-handlers.ts, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule, the API field and their tests; the only blemish is a release note that still describes the superseded furthest-from-zero rule.

maintainability.why: A single definition with a small options object is easy to own, though `op` is an untyped string and the desktop display callers (SchedulesTable, mobile list, useScheduleEdit) do not pass it, so approximate amounts show differently there than in Balance and the server paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All server and shared paths now call getScheduledAmount; no inline amount computation remains.

disguised_duplication.where: The previous copies were deleted and replaced by calls, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts gains an `op` option (with `inverse` moved into the same options object) and an `op === 'isapprox'` branch; this is the real variation of the rule rather than a caller-specific flag, and no call site re-implements the computation (display callers simply omit `op`).
